title: Do Not Give Up
story:
A farmer planted a small field with great care.

Every morning, he watered the soil and removed the weeds. He worked patiently, even though for many days he could not see much growth.

One morning, his son looked at the field and asked, "Why do you keep working so hard? Nothing seems to be happening."

The farmer smiled and said, "Just because you cannot see what is happening beneath the soil does not mean that nothing is happening. The seed is growing, even when you cannot see it."

The boy continued watching the field.

Weeks later, small green plants began to appear. With continued care, they eventually grew into a healthy harvest.

The farmer had learned something important: faithful work often produces results long before we can see them.

Galatians 6:9 encourages us not to become weary in doing good, because at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.

There are seasons in life when doing the right thing feels exhausting.

You may pray faithfully but still not see an answer.

You may serve others without receiving appreciation.

You may work hard toward a goal and see very little progress.

You may keep trying to improve your family, career, relationships, or spiritual life while wondering whether your efforts are making any difference.

In such moments, it is easy to become tired and think about giving up.

But God sees what you cannot see.

Every act of kindness matters.

Every prayer matters.

Every honest decision matters.

Every time you choose forgiveness instead of bitterness, patience instead of anger, and faithfulness instead of giving up, you are planting seeds.

You may not see the harvest immediately, but that does not mean your work is wasted.

A farmer cannot dig up a seed every day to check whether it is growing. He must plant it, care for it, and trust the process.

In the same way, God calls us to remain faithful even when results are not immediate.

This does not mean that we should continue doing something harmful or refuse to change our approach when wisdom tells us to adjust.

Perseverance includes learning, adapting, resting when necessary, and continuing to pursue what is right.

Sometimes the harvest comes in a form we did not expect.

You may pray for a situation to change, but God may first change your heart.

You may ask for success, but God may use the journey to develop your character.

You may want immediate results, but God may be building something that will last much longer.

Do not measure faithfulness only by visible results.

Some of the most important things God does in our lives happen quietly.

A child learning from your example.

A person encouraged by your kindness.

A relationship slowly being restored.

A habit of prayer becoming stronger.

A character being shaped through difficult circumstances.

You may not realize the impact today, but the seeds you plant can bear fruit in ways you cannot predict.

If you are tired today, take a moment to rest in God rather than abandoning the good work He has placed before you.

Ask Him for renewed strength.

Ask Him for wisdom to know what to continue, what to change, and what to release.

Then take the next faithful step.

You do not need to see the entire harvest today.

You only need to remain faithful with the seed in your hands.

The season of harvest belongs to God.

Your responsibility is to keep sowing what is good.

Keep praying.

Keep loving.

Keep serving.

Keep doing what is right.

Do not give up simply because you cannot yet see the results.

At the proper time, God can bring a harvest from the seeds of faithfulness you are planting today.
life_lesson: Do not give up when doing good becomes tiring or when results are slow. God sees your faithfulness even when you cannot see the harvest. Continue doing what is right, trust His timing, and allow Him to bring the results in His time.
prayer:
Dear Heavenly Father,

Thank You for reminding me not to become weary in doing good.

There are times when I feel tired because I do not see the results I hoped for.

When I become discouraged, remind me that You see what I cannot see.

Help me remain faithful even when my efforts seem unnoticed or unproductive.

Give me strength when I feel like giving up.

Give me wisdom to know when I should persevere, when I should change my approach, and when I need to rest.

Help me continue planting good seeds through my words, actions, prayers, and choices.

Teach me to be patient when the harvest does not come immediately.

When I serve others, help me do it with a sincere heart rather than looking for recognition.

When I work toward a goal, help me remain disciplined and faithful even when progress is slow.

Help me trust that no act of love, kindness, prayer, or obedience is wasted when it is done for You.

Protect me from discouragement, comparison, impatience, and the desire to quit too soon.

When I cannot see what You are doing, help me trust Your timing.

Renew my strength and give me the courage to take the next faithful step.

Help me remember that the harvest belongs to You.

May my life continue to produce good fruit that blesses others and brings glory to Your name.

Thank You for being faithful and for working even when I cannot see the results.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
reflection_question:
Where in your life are you feeling tired of doing what is right because you have not yet seen the results?

What good work or responsibility is God asking you to continue faithfully?

How can you trust God's timing instead of giving up too soon?
verse: Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
